question: Does the pinned default Kraken neural line segmenter provide a usable starting layout for real Voynich scans, compared with Kraken legacy boxes and at a lower resolution?

boxer.attribution: Alexander Boxer, independent transcription directly from Yale imagery. Notation is not EVA.

image_mapping.use: Only literal folio-to-canvas/image-service mapping; no semantic profile, plant identification, or model score used.

yale.institution: Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library, Yale University

positive.scope: One annotated historical page in a known script; control of geometry and software, not external validation of Voynich glyphs.

image_policy: Full canvas, no masks or result-dependent crops. Fetch Yale full/1800,/0/default.jpg once per page; resize the same bytes locally for 1200. Record URL, SHA256, dimensions, response status, bytes and exceptions. No OCR inference or training.

measurements.primary: sum(abs(predicted count - Boxer count)) / sum(Boxer count), on primary width. This is a count proxy, not spatial line accuracy.
measurements.paired_comparison: Neural primary count loss minus legacy primary count loss, descriptive only; no p-value for four selected pages.
measurements.robustness: Line count difference and one-to-one normalized-box IoU F1 between widths for each method. Stability is not correctness.
measurements.positive_control: One-to-one line bounding-box precision/recall/F1 against upstream PAGE-XML at IoU >= 0.5. GT normalized using XML dimensions; source image aspect ratio must agree within 2%. Annotation may have been seen during upstream model development, so this is not held-out model evaluation.
measurements.blank_control: Zero lines for each method on a uniform white image; documented empty-image rejection is acceptable for legacy binarization only.

gates.caveat: A PASS count proxy never means PASS segmentation accuracy, glyph recognition, language identification, or translation.

limits: Only first two leaves; no foldout/hand/section generalization.
Boxer transcribes block text; neural detections may include margins, foliation, or illustrations.
Count agreement can coexist with every geometric match being wrong.
No image-transcript assignment is automatically inferred from equal line counts.
Default blla API is deprecated in 7.1 but remains available and pinned; migrate before Kraken 8.
Package and model are pinned, but full transitive environment is recorded as installed rather than claimed byte-identical in advance.
